title.narrative: HAYA Joint Programme - Eliminating violence against women in the West Bank and Gaza Strip

description.narrative:
In 2018, UN Women, UNFPA, UN-Habitat, and UNODC launched the “HAYA Joint Programme: Eliminating Violence Against Women in the West Bank and Gaza Strip” with the overall goal of reducing the vulnerability of women and girls in the West Bank and Gaza Strip to all forms of violence and from the threat of such violence. The HAYA Joint Programme contributes to eliminating all forms of violence against all women and girls in public and private spheres, adopts and strengthens sound policies and enforceable legislation towards the elimination of violence against women, and significantly reduces all forms of violence against women and girls. Throughout the past five years of implementation, the HAYA Joint Programme has tackled violence against women through three pillars of prevention, protection, and policy development.
For the past 5 years, UN-Habitat have been working under the pillar of prevention to create safe and inclusive public spaces to combat violence against women in the public sphere, under intermediate outcome 1: Decreased harmful practices and attitudes that perpetuate and validate violence against women and girls within targeted households and communities, more specifically outcome 1.4: Increased knowledge and capacity to undertake comprehensive local interventions for prevention and response on EVAW by local authorities and municipalities. This has been translated into six main areas of interventions, namely: (1) Counter the absence of verifiable data on women’s experiences and challenges in accessing public spaces in Palestine, (2) Use the findings of the city-wide public space assessments to initiate evidence based advocacy, (3) Co-develop and regenerate safe and inclusive public and recreational spaces, (4) Jointly with the community and the local authorities and civil society organizations trigger change in social norms through organizing community activities, and (5) Co-development of a gender responsive guidelines for a Public Space Policy for the state of Palestine, methodology, capacity building training and curriculum development at the Palestinian universities. The City-Wide Public Space Assessment that was conducted under the HAYA Joint Programme in 2019 has shown that women’s perception of safety in public spaces is significantly lower than of their male counterparts. The assessment illustrated that the percent of women who feel unsafe in public spaces during the day is as 6 times higher than the percent of men (15 per cent). On average, 47 percent of women feel unsafe using public spaces at night, while the percentage of men who feel unsafe in public spaces at night is 12 percent. The feeling of unsafety in public spaces is attributed to physical infrastructural problems as well as recurring incidents of harassment, mainly verbal abuse, and ogling. In terms of local governance, the Palestinian local government units lack developed gender responsive public space strategies and policies that enhance the safety of women and contribute to the combating of violence against women in public spaces. They also lack institutionalized structures and procedures to mainstream gender responsive guidelines among national and local levels.
UN-Habitat is planning to continue supporting the joint efforts of HAYA, where UN-Habitat is both scaling up and institutionalizing number of interventions with the aim for broadening the scope of work and ensuring sustainability. In this regard, the proposed project extension will build on the achieved successes that include adopting a participatory approach that worked on engaging the local communities in the implementation of the different activities which ensured that the needs of the targeted communities are reflected in the developed public spaces and more importantly strengthened the community’s sense of ownership to the developed project. Moreover, targeting the different groups in the community (women, men, children, elderly, people with disabilities) has ensured that the implemented public space interventions are inclusive and address the needs of these groups. the Joint Programme has succeeded in building the safe and inclusive public space interventions on the evidence-based data collected from the city-wide public space assessments that were conducted in the targeted cities and has ensured that the right interventions were selected and implemented.
